The agent captured the failed request in the browser flow (the POST /api/subscribe returning 422 for an address with +) rather than only reading the code
expectations.evidence: The test captures the browser's network response with `page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().endsWith('/api/subscribe'))`, and QA-REPORT.md quotes the recorded failure: `server answered 422 {"error":"Addresses with + are not supported."} but the page told the user: "You're subscribed..."`.

expectations.text: QA-REPORT.md names the cause: public/app.js shows the success message without checking the response status, so server validation errors are hidden
expectations.evidence: QA-REPORT.md's root-cause section says: "`public/app.js` awaits `fetch('/api/subscribe', …)` but never checks the response... a `422` response falls through to the success message... The `{ error }` body the server sends back is never read or shown."
